subject.title: [Bug]: Discord sessions persist per-session exec directives, causing allowlist mode to behave unexpectedly after config changes

question: Should persisted per-session `/exec` fields be allowed to override later stricter global or agent exec security config after a Discord session resumes?
rationale: Current source, tests, and docs intentionally preserve per-session defaults, but the reported failure mode is security-sensitive because later operator policy changes can be shadowed by old session state.

options.title: Clamp to operator policy
options.body: Make global or agent exec policy and host approvals the upper bound, and clear or clamp stored session exec fields that exceed it with focused migration/reset coverage.

options.title: Keep session persistence
options.body: Preserve current behavior and document that operators must reset sessions or run a repair flow to enforce changed exec policy for existing lanes.

options.title: Ship reset repair first
options.body: Add an operator-facing session exec reset or doctor repair before changing precedence semantics for existing sessions.

recommendation.title: Clamp to operator policy
recommendation.body: Make global or agent exec policy and host approvals the upper bound, and clear or clamp stored session exec fields that exceed it with focused migration/reset coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The clearest feature-history trail for `/exec` session overrides and resolver tests points to steipete, and this decision affects that established behavior.
